subject: Workplace Skills
title: Intrinsic vs Extrinsic Motivation
description: A short lesson to help you apply Intrinsic vs Extrinsic Motivation.

hook.text: A nursery offered parents a fine for late pickups. Late arrivals doubled. The fine killed the guilt.

buildup.text: Extrinsic rewards like money and status work for simple tasks. For creative work, they often backfire.

discovery.text: Daniel Pink identified three intrinsic drivers: autonomy, mastery, and purpose. They sustain effort long-term.

twist.text: Adding external rewards to tasks people already enjoy can destroy the internal motivation completely.

climax.text: Pay people fairly, then focus on autonomy, growth, and meaning. That is what keeps talent engaged.

punchline.text: Pay enough to remove the issue. Then offer meaning.

quiz.question: What are Daniel Pink's three intrinsic motivators?
